key_constraints: Long-lived energy infrastructure requires affordable long-term finance
Grid equipment supply and installation capacity constrain delivery
Physical route risk and commodity benchmark prices can diverge
Emerging-market borrowing costs and fiscal capacity differ materially

producer_checks.information_cutoff: 19 Nov 2026 07:45 BRT / 10:45 UTC. The IEA World Energy Outlook 2026 is dated 19 Nov; exact public release hour is not stated, while the producer's embargo advisory records 08:00 Antalya / 05:00 UTC. Reuters's US market report [4] was published at 10:28 UTC, before this revised cutoff. Market closes refer to 18 Nov. The Reuters 04:55 GMT oil quote and the Asian 03:51 GMT snapshot are intraday observations, not closes.
producer_checks.novelty: Compared with 16 Nov (China/Japan activity and dollar funding), 17 Nov (semiconductor repricing and Brazil activity/inflation expectations), and 18 Nov (European inflation and AI financing), this edition uses the newly dated IEA World Energy Outlook 2026 to quantify energy-security capital requirements: bypass pipeline scenarios, grid kilometres, equipment bottlenecks, importer investment and emerging-market financing constraints. It does not repeat the previous edition's AI-contract analysis.
producer_checks.evidence_vintage: IEA WEO 2026 is a scenario report dated 19 Nov, not a realised project pipeline. IEA Oil Market Report is dated 13 Nov. EIA petroleum stocks refer to the week ended 13 Nov and report released 18 Nov. Treasury curve, equity closes, FX and gold observations refer to 18 Nov; Reuters preliminary US index values were published 19 Nov at 10:28 UTC. Asian quotes are a delayed intraday snapshot at 03:51 GMT on 19 Nov. Eurostat October HICP is a final release published 18 Nov. World Bank debt figures refer to 2025.
producer_checks.bilingual_parity: EN and PT-BR use the same 13 references, dates, quantitative observations, scenario conditions, charts, tables, map regions, flow stages and epistemic qualifications. US index values are explicitly labelled as Reuters preliminary data in both editions; the AP comparison was removed to avoid mixing preliminary and final market-data vintages. The cyberattack and natural-hazard outage wording distinguishes attacks targeting utilities from confirmed outages.
producer_checks.visual_evidence: Two explicit bar charts, three evidence tables, one regional map and one causal flow. Values and labels are matched across EN/PT-BR; scenarios are not charted as observations.
producer_checks.source_limitations: No harmonised same-date global private credit-spread series, project-finance margins, delivered diesel prices or verified project-level grid capex/disbursements were established for this edition.

reconciliation.note: All seven active reconciliation-required assets were reviewed; no canonical dataset update was supported by the evidence in this brief.

revision_2_corrections.correction: Moved the declared cutoff and planned publication time to 07:45 BRT / 10:45 UTC, after Reuters [4] at 10:28 UTC; explicitly labelled the index observations as Reuters preliminary data; removed AP [14] because it reports a different close vintage; updated the Reuters [2] headline to match the current source page.

limitations: The exact publication hour of the IEA World Energy Outlook 2026 is not stated on its 19 November page.
IEA scenarios and system requirements are modelled pathways, not realised infrastructure, committed capital or guaranteed policy outcomes.
The 7 mb/d pipeline figure includes projects under construction or consideration; the Low Hormuz Case depends on multiple conditional assumptions.
US EIA inventories are a national weekly observation and cannot establish global diesel availability.
Treasury par yields do not measure private credit spreads, project-finance margins or sovereign borrowing spreads.
The Asian equity figures are delayed intraday observations at 03:51 GMT, not closing returns.
The World Bank debt aggregates are not energy-project debt and do not identify the financing terms of individual infrastructure projects.
The Brazil market move reflects domestic fiscal uncertainty as well as external dollar and rate conditions.
contrary_evidence: Brent and WTI fell on 18 November and US commercial crude inventories rose in the week ended 13 November, consistent with a looser near-term crude balance.
The IEA expects oil supply to rebound in 2027, which could lower benchmark prices if the forecast materialises.
India's rupee remained resilient despite a stronger dollar, with reported November equity inflows supporting the currency.
US crude and distillate inventories increased in the latest weekly EIA balance, even while the IEA describes low global on-land stocks and tight diesel markets.
The IEA's grid and pipeline figures are system requirements and scenario assumptions, not proof of project bankability or implementation.

en.title: Global Macro — Energy security turns the Hormuz shock into a global capital-allocation test
en.deck: The IEA's new outlook quantifies the capital, equipment and financing needed to diversify energy supply and expand electricity grids, even as crude prices soften.
en.regime: Energy-security repricing and accelerated electrification under elevated dollar rates and uneven access to long-duration capital.
en.key_risk: Lower crude prices may ease near-term inflation without resolving grid, equipment, route and financing constraints that determine delivered energy reliability.
